<explanation>
Based on the provided file tree and README, I'll explain how to create a comprehensive system design diagram for Audiobookshelf, a self-hosted audiobook and podcast server application.

1. Main Components to Include:

a. Frontend Layer:
- Vue.js/Nuxt.js based web client (/client directory)
- Progressive Web App (PWA) capabilities
- Mobile apps (Android/iOS) integration points
- Web socket connections for real-time updates

b. Backend Layer:
- Node.js server (/server directory)
- Core server components (Server.js, Auth.js, Database.js)
- Controllers for different functionalities
- Managers for specific features
- File system handlers

c. Storage Layer:
- Database storage (SQLite/embedded)
- File system storage for media files
- Backup storage system
- Cache management system

d. External Services Integration:
- Metadata providers (Audible, Google Books, etc.)
- RSS feed services
- Email services
- Chromecast integration

2. Key Relationships to Highlight:

a. Data Flow:
- Client-server communication via REST API and WebSocket
- Media streaming pathways
- Metadata synchronization
- User authentication flow

b. Component Interactions:
- Library scanning and monitoring
- Media processing pipeline
- Backup and restoration processes
- Podcast feed management

3. Architectural Patterns to Emphasize:

- MVC pattern in the backend structure
- Component-based architecture in the frontend
- Event-driven architecture for real-time updates
- Service-oriented architecture for external integrations

4. Diagram Structure:

```
[Client Layer]
   |
   |- Web Client (Vue.js/Nuxt.js)
   |- Mobile Apps
   |- Progressive Web App
   |
[API Gateway / WebSocket]
   |
[Server Layer]
   |
   |- Authentication & Authorization
   |- Core Services
   |  |- Library Management
   |  |- Media Processing
   |  |- User Management
   |  |- Podcast Management
   |
   |- Support Services
   |  |- Backup Manager
   |  |- Cache Manager
   |  |- Task Manager
   |  |- Notification Manager
   |
[Storage Layer]
   |
   |- Database (SQLite)
   |- File System
   |- Cache Storage
   |
[External Services]
   |- Metadata Providers
   |- RSS Feeds
   |- Email Services
   |- Chromecast
```

5. Color Coding:

- Blue: Client-side components
- Green: Server-side core components
- Yellow: Storage components
- Purple: External services
- Red: Security/Authentication components
- Orange: Support services

6. Important Implementation Details:

- Show the separation between the client (/client) and server (/server) codebases
- Highlight the managers (/server/managers) that handle specific functionality
- Include the controllers (/server/controllers) that manage API endpoints
- Show the model structure (/server/models) for data organization
- Indicate the providers (/server/providers) for external service integration

7. Additional Considerations:

- Include the migration system for database updates
- Show the backup/restore workflow
- Indicate the scanning/monitoring system for library updates
- Display the media processing pipeline for different file types
- Show the localization system integration

Remember to:
- Keep the diagram clean and readable
- Use consistent styling
- Include a clear legend
- Add brief descriptions for complex interactions
- Show both synchronous and asynchronous communication paths

This system design should provide a clear understanding of how Audiobookshelf's components work together while maintaining the right level of detail for a principal software engineer to understand the system architecture.
